taskVersion.name: ves-synthetic-a-item

parts.text:
Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station T-05, survey area T. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 1320.7 | 0.60 | 0.60
2 | 719.2 | 0.46 | 1.06
3 | 872.7 | 0.61 | 1.67
4 | 340.7 | 0.38 | 2.05
5 | 4088.9 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as HKH-type.

Is this label correct for these layer values? Give a short answer, then end with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"label_correct": true or false, "curve_type": "<letters>"}

To determine the curve type for the 5-layer model, we evaluate each consecutive 3-layer triplet:

1. **Layers 1-2-3:** $\rho_1 = 1320.7 > \rho_2 = 719.2 < \rho_3 = 872.7 \rightarrow \mathbf{H}$
2. **Layers 2-3-4:** $\rho_2 = 719.2 < \rho_3 = 872.7 > \rho_4 = 340.7 \rightarrow \mathbf{K}$
3. **Layers 3-4-5:** $\rho_3 = 872.7 > \rho_4 = 340.7 < \rho_5 = 4088.9 \rightarrow \mathbf{H}$

Combining these yields **HKH**, which matches the interpretation on file.

{"label_correct": true, "curve_type": "HKH"}
